semantic_changes: Both events now carry the case label phantom_restart; the case event adds a phase field set to commit. No measurement changed.

scope.description: One three-node in-memory cluster in which A and B are the committed voters and C has no configuration; the leader injects a store failure on the AddVoter(C) write, loses contact with the other committed voter, commits a client command with the phantom quorum, is shut down, and is replaced by a fresh Raft over the same stores.
assumptions: The failure is injected for exactly the next StoreLogs call, so only the configuration entry is lost.
C stays reachable while the other committed voter is cut, which is what allows the phantom quorum of two to be satisfied.
The restart uses the leader's own store, snapshot store, transport and configuration, so it re-reads exactly what that node persisted.
Both events carry the same case label so that the prerequisite and the result correlate; the phase field distinguishes the commit half from the restart half.
excluded: No variation of the number of restarts or of the cluster size.
No assertion about what happens if the retained entry is later replicated to the committed peer.
No snapshot is taken before the restart, so the replay is over the full stored log.

basis.prefix: The harness bootstraps A and B with the two-voter configuration, starts C with no configuration, waits for a leader among A and B, marks the leader's store to fail the next StoreLogs call, and calls AddVoter(C). It then disconnects the leader from the other committed voter, waits for the leader to remain leader, applies one command and records the commit index together with the committed peer's last index. The case event carries case phantom_restart, phase commit, and records the add error, the latest configuration index, the last stored index, the phantom voter count and the apply result. The leader is shut down, a fresh Raft is created over the same store, snapshot store and transport, and the result event carries the same case label and records the configuration error, the loaded server list and voter count, whether the new server is present, the last stored index and the stored commit index.
basis.responsibility: The library decides whether a configuration entry is installed in memory and what it reports to the caller, and it decides which configuration a node adopts when it starts. A configuration whose write failed was never given a place in the log, so a restart must reconstruct authority from the log alone.

comparisons.description: A configuration entry whose write failed was never stored, so the restarted node must not load it; a true witness would make the defect durable rather than process-local.

knowledge.assertion: appendConfigurationEntry installs the new configuration in memory regardless of whether its log entry was stored.
quorumSize, electSelf and setupLeaderState derive voter sets from the latest configuration.
